text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 1.4% today, extending a sharp 7% decline over two weeks. The timing aligns with a major shift in market sentiment: energy analysts are calling the "epic boom in refinery-related stocks" over, signaling that the exceptionally profitable window for refiners is closing. Refinery margins depend on the spread between crude oil prices and finished fuel prices, and that gap has been compressing as crude and refined products move in sync.

The broader backdrop reinforces this unwinding. Oil remains in the $89–$93 range globally, refinery utilization is very high at 95.7%, and fuel inventories are substantial—conditions that typically cap margin expansion. Meanwhile, climate talks have collapsed without commitments to curb fossil fuels, removing any near-term tailwind for energy prices or sentiment, and Middle East tensions continue but haven't pushed oil materially higher, suggesting markets aren't pricing in sustained supply disruption.
